papers.summary: Adds an SVD-free Rényi-2 effective-rank penalty to LoRA. In mixed-domain rank sweeps, it improves mean Wiki perplexity over unpenalized LoRA at tested ranks of at least 16, though retention gains depend on configuration.
papers.relevance: Directly tests whether spectral regularization changes adapter capacity and fine-tuning quality.

evidence.quote: a penalty weight of λ = 0.01 \\lambda=0.01 lowers mean Wiki perplexity at every tested rank of at least 16 16 relative to unpenalized LoRA.
the penalty can improve retention without a large training-fit cost, but does not eliminate the learning–forgetting trade-off.

papers.title: Maximizing Capacity Utilization of LoRA Adapters for Mitigating the Learning-Forgetting Trade-off

papers.summary: Shows that low stable rank need not imply that a language-model weight update is easy to approximate at low rank. Selected PPO attention updates have stable ranks of 9.6–18.3 but need 532–1,222 components to retain 80% of their energy.
papers.relevance: Provides a caution for interpreting singular-value diagnostics in work on weight-update compressibility.

evidence.quote: Three attention updates from proximal policy optimization (PPO) have stable ranks 9.6 9.6 – 18.3 18.3 but require 532 532 – 1,222 1{,}222 components for 80 % 80\\% of their energy.
Thus, low stable rank alone does not generally imply that a small number of singular components captures most of the update energy.

papers.title: Spectral Rank and Step-Direction Dynamics in Language-Model Post-Training

papers.summary: FOAM simplifies SOAP’s preconditioning and second-moment state. Across 124M–760M-parameter LLM pretraining experiments, it approaches SOAP’s validation loss with half its optimizer state, while SOAP retains the lowest loss.
papers.relevance: Directly informs quality, memory, and wall-clock tradeoffs for matrix-structured pretraining optimizers.

evidence.quote: SOAP attains the lowest validation loss at every scale, with FOAM behind by 0.004 0.004 , 0.008 0.008 , and 0.005 0.005 nats at small, medium, and large, each within about one seed std.
FOAM uses half of SOAP’s matrix-parameter state at every size, and its measured peak memory at small size is + 7.4 % +7.4\\% over AdamW against + 12.9 % +12.9\\% for SOAP.

papers.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP

papers.summary: SCALAR learns scalar coefficients over fixed, task-calibrated directions. On Qwen2.5-7B commonsense fine-tuning, it reports LoRA-comparable accuracy with fewer trainable parameters, 20% lower peak memory, and 6% higher throughput.
papers.relevance: A practical PEFT comparison spanning adaptation quality, training memory, and throughput.

evidence.quote: On commonsense reasoning, SCALAR achieves accuracy comparable to LoRA with about 4% of its trainable parameters.
SCALAR achieves the lowest peak memory among the evaluated PEFT methods, using 20% less memory than LoRA, 15% less than NOLA, and 33% less than RandLoRA. Training throughput increases by 6% over LoRA

papers.title: Direction or Magnitude? Learning Scalars over Task-Calibrated Directions

papers.summary: HiLo synchronizes distributed LoRA rollout workers through compressed gradients and optimizer replay rather than transmitting adapters. Spar combines spectral truncation and adaptive rank allocation; reported gains apply to bandwidth-constrained post-training.
papers.relevance: Addresses the user’s explicit interest in separating LoRA training rank from communication cost without sacrificing much learning quality.

evidence.quote: HiLo replaces parameter transmission with compressed gradient dissemination and local optimizer replay, reducing synchronization traffic without lowering the training rank.

HiLo with Spar maintains learning quality close to full synchronization while transmitting as little as 1.6% of the adapter bytes, and accelerates end-to-end updates by up to 2.2 × 2.2\\times under bandwidth constraints.

papers.title: Train High, Ship Low: Efficient LoRA Synchronization for Distributed On-Policy Post-Training

papers.summary: Compares AdamW, AdaGrad, SOAP, two feasible Shampoo reductions, and All-2D Muon in fixed-budget Qwen KL distillation. Matrix-structured recipes do not consistently improve validation-KL versus trainer-time tradeoffs over elementwise baselines.
papers.relevance: Useful counterpoint when deciding whether optimizer gains observed in pretraining transfer to another LLM training objective and systems regime.

evidence.quote: Across scales, none of the evaluated matrix-structured recipes consistently improves the quality–trainer-time trade-off over the elementwise references: AdamW generally attains the lowest validation KL, while AdaGrad can be slightly faster at larger scale.
The findings therefore do not rank optimizer families independently of factorization, routing, and implementation.

papers.title: Do Pretraining Optimizer Gains Transfer to KL Distillation?

papers.summary: Surveys how LLM post-training shapes information-seeking decisions, including retrieval routing, query refinement, tool exploration, and evidence use.
papers.relevance: Directly informs search-control and evidence-handling decisions in the user’s research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: This paper organizes research around six interrelated information-seeking capabilities and examines the learning signals, optimization methods, update loci, and credit-assignment mechanisms used to develop them.

Existing studies report gains in retrieval routing, query refinement, multi-tool exploration, evidence-grounded reasoning, and resource-aware search, although the scope of behavioral evidence varies across capabilities.

papers.title: From Search to Decision: How Post-Training Shapes Information-Seeking Capabilities in Large Language Models

limitations: These are reported paper findings, not independently replicated results; code availability was not checked.
FOAM’s main comparison reaches 760M parameters, and its authors identify larger-scale pretraining as an open question.
HiLo’s speedup is conditional on bandwidth constraints and requires replicated optimizer state at rollout workers.
The KL-distillation study measures teacher-matching KL, not downstream performance or pretraining, and its conclusions depend on the evaluated implementations.
The information-seeking paper is a survey, not a direct evaluation of a research-digest agent.
